title: The early web
summary: Browsers, search, publishing, commerce, news, and shared knowledge from the web’s beginnings through 2005.

entries.title: The first website
entries.note: CERN’s restored November 1992 edition of the first website, served today.

entries.title: NCSA Mosaic
entries.note: The browser project that helped bring the graphical web to a broad audience.

entries.title: Netscape
entries.note: A commercial browser and server company during the first browser boom.

entries.title: Mozilla
entries.note: An open browser project growing out of Netscape, later releasing Firefox.

entries.title: World Wide Web Consortium
entries.note: Open standards for a web that could work across browsers and institutions.

entries.title: Internet Archive
entries.note: The web-preservation project in 1997, then public access through the Wayback Machine in 2002.

entries.title: Electronic Frontier Foundation
entries.note: Digital civil liberties, free expression, and the struggle over who controls the network.

entries.title: Microsoft
entries.note: Windows and Internet Explorer during the competition to control the browser.

entries.title: Apple
entries.note: Apple in late 1996 and early 2001, then its home page just after the first iPod announcement.

entries.title: Linux Online
entries.note: The public face of a free operating system built by a distributed developer community.

entries.title: GNU Project
entries.note: Free software, its licenses, and the tools behind much of the web’s infrastructure.

entries.title: SourceForge
entries.note: Shared hosting and collaboration for open-source software projects.

entries.title: Yahoo!
entries.note: A human-edited web directory becoming a mass-market portal.

entries.title: AltaVista
entries.note: Full-text search at a scale that helped make the growing web navigable.

entries.title: WebCrawler
entries.note: An early service for searching the words within web pages.

entries.title: Open Directory Project
entries.note: Volunteer editors organizing the web into a shared directory.

entries.title: Google
entries.note: The beta search page and its later, spare front door to the web.

entries.title: Amazon.com
entries.note: The online retailer in 2000, with books, music, toys, electronics, and third-party shops.

entries.title: eBay
entries.note: Person-to-person auctions making an online marketplace out of everyday possessions.

entries.title: craigslist
entries.note: Local classifieds in its short-lived ListFoundation era, then a growing network of city pages.

entries.title: Pets.com
entries.note: A heavily promoted dot-com retailer before and during its closure in 2000.

entries.title: eToys: closure notice
entries.note: The toy retailer’s 2001 closure notice, with its explanation of the failed business.

entries.title: HotWired
entries.note: A publication made for the web, combining technology, design, culture, and advertising.

entries.title: Salon
entries.note: A web-native magazine building an audience for journalism and cultural criticism.

entries.title: Suck: predictions for 1997
entries.note: A 1997 capture of Suck’s 26 December 1996 predictions about the web.

entries.title: GeoCities
entries.note: Free personal home pages organized into virtual neighborhoods; this is the service’s front page.

entries.title: The WELL
entries.note: The public entrance to an influential discussion community that began before the web.

entries.title: Slashdot
entries.note: Reader-submitted technology news and sprawling public discussion.

entries.title: Blogger
entries.note: Simple publishing tools helping personal weblogs reach a wider audience.

entries.title: LiveJournal
entries.note: Personal journals connected through friends, comments, and community.

entries.title: MetaFilter
entries.note: A community weblog built around interesting links and conversation.

entries.title: Wikipedia
entries.note: The encyclopedia’s first year, as volunteers began writing and revising articles together.

entries.title: Project Gutenberg
entries.note: A volunteer digital library of freely available books, older than the web itself.

entries.title: American Memory
entries.note: The Library of Congress bringing historical documents, photographs, and sound to the web.

entries.title: Internet Movie Database
entries.note: A collaboratively assembled film reference that grew from an online fan community.

entries.title: Exploratorium
entries.note: A science museum using the web for exhibits and experiments beyond its building.

entries.title: NASA
entries.note: NASA’s temporary Pathfinder mirror list, helping readers reach the 1997 Mars landing coverage.

entries.title: Mars Pathfinder: landing-site guide
entries.note: A landing-site guide from the Mars Pathfinder mission, shown in a 1999 capture.

entries.title: The Trojan Room coffee pot
entries.note: The Cambridge webcam’s explanatory page: an everyday coffee pot became a destination on the early web.

entries.title: The New York Times
entries.note: The newspaper’s public web entrance in 1996; registration and linked articles are outside this saved page.

entries.title: BBC News
entries.note: BBC News in 1998, then its front page on 12 September 2001.

entries.title: CNN
entries.note: CNN’s continuous web news service in 2000, then its front page on 12 September 2001.

entries.title: The White House
entries.note: The Clinton administration’s final home page, then the incoming George W. Bush administration.

entries.title: Yahoo! Japan
entries.note: A Japanese-language directory and portal; language shaped how people found their way online.

entries.title: Universo Online
entries.note: A Portuguese-language portal bringing news, services, and publishing together in Brazil.

entries.title: Sina
entries.note: A Chinese-language portal bringing news, search, shopping, and communities together.

entries.title: Naver
entries.note: A Korean-language search and portal service in its early years.

entries.title: Rediff
entries.note: An Indian news and services portal during the country’s early public-web era.

entries.title: Al Jazeera
entries.note: An Arabic-language news service reaching readers beyond broadcast television.

entries.title: Space Jam
entries.note: The surviving 1996 film-site edition, hosted at a later address and served today.
